# IEUM Concierge

> IEUM Concierge (이음, Korean for "a joining" or "connection") is a private luxury wellness travel concierge based between Seoul and New York. It plans, books, and runs fully bespoke journeys through Korea end to end, across Seoul, Jeju, Busan, Gyeongju, and the regions between, and also plans corporate events in Korea and advises Korean brands entering Europe and the United States.

Wellness sits at the centre of every journey IEUM designs. It is not one option among several. Korea's culture, beauty, and cuisine are woven through it, whatever shape the trip takes: a family holiday, a milestone celebration, or time alone. Because IEUM handles the researching, routing, planning, and booking, and stays reachable throughout, clients take a true vacation and come home rested, refreshed, and rejuvenated, with no need for a second holiday to recover from the first.

Founded by Doha Yoon. Every itinerary is designed individually and never sold as a package. IEUM works most often with travelers from Europe, the United States, and Latin America. Everything is delivered in English and Korean, with French and Spanish speaking guides arranged on request. Services include private drivers, personal translators, expert cultural guides, restaurant and experience reservations that are not available to book online, and 24 hour concierge support for the duration of a trip.

IEUM works across the whole of Korea, not only Seoul. Journeys run in Seoul, Jeju, Busan, Gyeongju, Sokcho, and the smaller places between them, in every season, for stays from a few days to a few weeks.

## Services

- [Private Journeys](https://ie-um.com/private-journeys): Fully bespoke luxury itineraries through Korea, planned, booked, and run end to end. Wellness is at the centre of every journey: temple stays in the mountains, hot spring towns, jjimjilbang bathhouse traditions, and the quieter regions where Koreans go to rest, from Seoraksan to Jeju. Woven through it are Korea's culture (hanbok at the palaces, artisan workshops, private museum visits), beauty (hanbang facials, dermatology clinics, Seoul styling studios), and cuisine (restaurants that do not take online reservations, royal cuisine cooking classes, market mornings). Journeys then take the shape of the occasion: Family Journeys built for travelling with children, including dietary needs, accessibility and split day planning; Milestone Journeys for proposals, anniversaries and birthdays; and Solo and Couple Journeys for restorative time away. Every journey includes itinerary design and booking, a private driver, personal translator, private cultural guide, and 24 hour concierge support.
- [Corporate Events](https://ie-um.com/corporate-events): IEUM works in two directions for companies in Korea. The first is corporate travel: wellness led executive retreats, incentive travel and off sites for a company's own people, with rest built into the programme rather than added to it. The second is corporate event management for brands: small client facing events in Korea such as private client dinners for eight to thirty guests, collection launches and previews, press and partner evenings, and VIP hosting for visiting executives. Both include venue sourcing, negotiated group accommodation, transport, professional translation, on site coordination, and themed events, across Seoul, Busan, Jeju and the regions between.
- [Consulting](https://ie-um.com/consulting): Market entry consulting for Korean brands expanding into Europe and the United States. Covers branding and marketing strategy, go to market strategy and planning, and local operations and recruitment.

## Signature journeys

- [Korean Temple Cuisine](https://ie-um.com/journeys/temple-cuisine): A private plant based journey through sachal eumsik, Korean Buddhist temple food. It uses no meat or fish and also excludes the five pungent vegetables, osinchae: garlic, onion, spring onion, chive and wild chive, which are held to stir desire and disturb meditation. Flavour comes from soy sauce, doenjang and gochujang fermented at the temple, some aged for decades. IEUM arranges cooking and eating with monastic chefs at Baekyangsa in Jangseong, where Jeong Kwan of Netflix's Chef's Table is abbess of the Cheonjinam hermitage, at Jingwansa inside Bukhansan National Park on the edge of Seoul, and at the Korean Temple Food Center near Jogyesa in central Seoul. Korean temple food is vegan by definition and predates the term by centuries.
- [Korea in Autumn](https://ie-um.com/journeys/autumn-foliage): A private Korea autumn foliage journey. Korean autumn colour moves from north to south over roughly six weeks: Seoraksan peaks from late September to mid October, the central mountains such as Odaesan through mid to late October, the southern sites including Naejangsan, Jirisan and Gyeongju from late October to early November, and Seoul last in early to mid November. IEUM tracks the foliage front and adjusts the route while clients are already travelling, and secures the timed limited tickets for the Secret Garden at Changdeokgung. Six months ahead is comfortable to book, three months is tight.
- [Sound, and the Making of It](https://ie-um.com/journeys/sound-and-craft): A private Korean sound wellness journey. The geomungo is a low six string zither struck with a bamboo stick and the gayageum is plucked and higher. Korean court music, jeongak, is played at a deliberately slow tempo tied to the breathing of the listener, which suits rest and not performance. The journey includes visiting workshops where instruments are still cut, hollowed, strung and lacquered by hand, a short private gayageum lesson, ganggangsullae, the women's circle dance from Jindo and Haenam inscribed by UNESCO on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity and traditionally danced under a full moon at harvest, and a closing sound bath of about an hour played on Korean traditional instruments.

- [Luxury Shopping in Seoul](https://ie-um.com/guides/luxury-shopping-in-seoul): Where to shop in Seoul district by district (Cheongdam, Apgujeong Rodeo, Hannam-dong and Seongsu), the major department stores (Shinsegae Gangnam, the highest grossing single department store in Korea at roughly 3.67 trillion won in 2025; Galleria in Apgujeong, open since 1990 and the first Korean department store to carry Chanel, Hermes and Louis Vuitton; and The Hyundai Seoul, which reached 100 million visitors within 30 months of opening), hanbok made to order (Danha Seoul by Kim Dan-ha, who made the hanbok Jennie and Rose wore in BLACKPINK's How You Like That; Tchai Kim by Kim Young-jin; Leesle by Hwang Yi-seul for everyday hanbok; and traditional masters such as Park Sul-nyeo who will cut a wedding gown in the hanbok line), Korean designers including Wooyoungmi, Gentle Monster, Tamburins, Ader Error, Andersson Bell and Low Classic, where to buy Korean beauty (Olive Young, Daiso, Musinsa, pharmacies and department store beauty halls), how the Korean tax refund works (10 percent VAT, immediate refund between 15,000 and 1,000,000 won per receipt up to 5,000,000 won per stay), and IEUM's private personal shopper service in Seoul.

## Common questions answered on this site

- Do I need a visa to visit Korea? Most travellers, including citizens of the United States, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand, can currently enter Korea without a K-ETA through 31 December 2026 under a temporary exemption covering 67 countries. An e-Arrival card is still required within three days of arrival.
- How many days should I plan for a first visit to Korea? Ten days is a comfortable minimum to see Seoul, Busan, and Jeju without rushing, though shorter well designed itineraries work well with a concierge handling logistics.
- What is the best time of year to visit Korea? Spring brings cherry blossoms in April, autumn brings foliage in October and November, and winter is the season for hot springs and quieter travel.
- Is tipping expected in Korea? No. Tipping is not customary anywhere in Korea, including restaurants, taxis, and hotels.
- How is IEUM different from a travel agent? A travel agent books what already exists. IEUM designs what does not, opening access through relationships built over years in Korea.
- How far in advance should I book? Four to six weeks gives the best access to reservations and experiences that fill early, though shorter timelines are regularly accommodated.
